prompt.context: Your client is A-Plus School District (APSD), a large public school district in the Southeast United States. APSD's superintendent has been concerned about complaints from parents and community leaders regarding unacceptable student test scores on the end-of-year exams. The superintendent has engaged your firm to recommend changes to improve student test scores and ensure all students are academically successful.
prompt.question: What changes would you recommend to improve student test scores and ensure all students at APSD are academically successful?

clarifying_info.q: How many students does APSD serve?
clarifying_info.a: APSD serves a little over 38,000 students.
Students in 3rd through 10th grade take end-of-year exams. Kindergarten, 1st, 11th, and 12th grade do not take the assessment.
Proficiency is defined as a student meeting 70% or more of the learning objectives for their grade level.

clarifying_info.q: What is the school grade-band configuration?
clarifying_info.a: Elementary school covers 1st-4th grade, middle school covers 5th-8th grade, and high school covers 9th-12th grade.

clarifying_info.q: How quickly does the superintendent want changes implemented?
clarifying_info.a: The superintendent wants to implement changes as quickly as possible.

exhibits.title: Student Proficiency Rates by Grade, Subject, and Year
exhibits.shows: A table showing the percentage of students scoring proficient or advanced on end-of-year exams at APSD for grades 3 through 10, broken down by subject (Reading, Math, Science) and year (2018, 2019, 2020).

exhibits.title: Student and Teacher Counts by Grade Band and District
exhibits.shows: A table comparing APSD, Rosebud, and Silver Springs school districts on number of students and number of teachers across the three grade bands (1st-4th, 5th-8th, 9th-12th).

exhibits.title: Budget Allocation by Category and Grade Band
exhibits.shows: A table showing each budget category (Academics, Teacher salaries, Administration, Athletics, Arts and activities, Transportation, Building/maintenance, Building construction, Other) as a percentage of total budget for each grade band (1st-4th, 5th-8th, 9th-12th) at APSD.

framework: In-School Factors: Teacher quality (experience, certification, training), student-to-teacher ratio, student schedule optimization, tutoring programs, discipline issues, curriculum quality, IEP/disability accommodations, ESOL/language considerations, spending optimization focused on direct student learning impact

Outside-School Factors: Parental involvement (understanding content, helping with homework), community organization involvement, internet access for students, student commitments outside school (family care, jobs), extracurriculars (sports, arts, religion)

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, what insights can you draw about student achievement at APSD?
questions.guidance: A basic response identifies that grades 5-8 (middle school) are experiencing the most significant and worsening performance issues across all three subjects, while grades 3-4 and 9-10 perform reasonably well. An advanced response recognizes that grades 5-8 map exactly to the middle school grade band, suggesting a systemic school-level issue rather than subject-specific or individual teacher problems. The hypothesis to investigate further should focus on what is structurally different about the middle school band — e.g., student-to-teacher ratio, administrative support, curriculum transition.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 2 (student enrollment and teacher counts by grade band), what inference can you draw about APSD?
questions.guidance: The candidate should calculate student-to-teacher ratios for each grade band and compare across districts. APSD's 5th-8th grade ratio of 23:1 is notably higher than the 20:1 benchmark seen in Rosebud, Silver Springs, and APSD's own other grade bands. This supports the hypothesis that understaffing in the middle school band is contributing to poor outcomes. Next steps should include examining how to adjust teacher distribution or hire additional teachers for 5th-8th grade.

math.setup: Divide number of students by number of teachers for each grade band and district.
math.answer: APSD 5th-8th grade has a student-to-teacher ratio of 23:1, versus 20:1 for all other grade bands and comparable districts.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3 and the budget information provided, how could APSD fund additional teachers for the 5th-8th grade band, and is it feasible to bring the ratio down to 20:1?
questions.guidance: A basic response suggests reallocating budget toward teacher salaries for 5th-8th grade. A strong response uses the raw dollar amounts ($60M for grades 5-8) and identifies the Administration line (17% vs. 10% in other bands) as the primary source of reallocation. The candidate should quantify how many teachers can be hired and whether that achieves 20:1. They should also identify risks of reducing the admin budget (more discipline issues, less teacher feedback, slower school-wide issue resolution).

math.setup: Reallocate 7% of the 5th-8th grade admin budget to teacher salaries. Annual budget for 5th-8th grade is $60M. Each new teacher costs $50K/year.
steps: New teachers that can be hired: $4.2M / $50K = 84 teachers
math.answer: Redirecting 7% of the 5th-8th grade administration budget frees $4.2M, enough to hire 84 new teachers and bring the student-to-teacher ratio from 23:1 down to 20:1.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors inside and outside of school could be driving low student test scores?

categories.name: In-School Factors
ideas: Teacher quality: experience, certification, and training completed
Tutoring programs available to struggling students
Curriculum quality and alignment to standards
ESOL and English language learner support
Spending optimization — focusing budget on items that directly impact student learning

categories.name: Outside-School Factors
ideas: Parental involvement: parents' understanding of content and ability to help with homework
Community organization involvement in student support
Internet access for students to complete assignments
Student commitments outside school (caring for siblings, part-time jobs)

recommendation: Recommend that APSD reallocate 7% of the 5th-8th grade administration budget to teacher salaries, freeing $4.2M to hire 84 new teachers and reduce the middle school student-to-teacher ratio from 23:1 to 20:1, bringing it in line with comparable districts and APSD's own other grade bands.
risks: Impact of reducing the administration budget: potential layoffs, slowed operations, and reduced administrative capacity
Supply and quality of teachers: it may be challenging to find and hire qualified teachers for 5th-8th grade quickly
Timing: recruiting, hiring, and onboarding 84 teachers takes time and may delay impact
Fewer admins may lead to more discipline issues and less frequent feedback for teachers
School-wide operational issues may take longer to resolve with reduced administrative staff
next_steps: Determine which administrative positions could be reduced without adversely impacting student learning or school operations
Work with the school board to approve the hiring plan and budget reallocation
Explore additional levers such as professional development for existing teachers, tutoring programs, and curriculum improvements in parallel
